title.narrative: NIHR-HSPR-PA-Schema-Uganda: Strengthening community health and epidemic management in Uganda

description.narrative: This project has 2 objectives: 1. To establish how Uganda's community health system can be strengthened to optimise resource allocation, improve outbreak preparedness, and enhance delivery of routine and emergency services. 2. To establish how stakeholder engagement, supported by participatory modelling, can facilitate evidence-informed decision-making and strengthen policy coalitions for community health systems in Uganda.

This project is a three year, mixed-methods research programme that aims to strengthen community health systems and epidemic preparedness in Uganda by integrated governance analysis, knowledge mobilisation, and participatory modelling. Organised into three interlinked workstreams, the study examines how different configurations of community health systems and community health workers perform during routine service delivery and during epidemic response, and how these can be optimised for efficiency, equity, and resilience.
The work is led by a multidisciplinary team of Ugandan and UK researchers, with expertise in health systems research, epidemiology, economics, and modelling, working at Makere University, Uganda and University of York, UK. Working in close collaboration with the Ministry of Health, district health teams, community health supervisors, community health workers, civil society organisations, and development partners. Stakeholders are engaged not only as respondents but as active contributors through participatory dialogue, capacity-building, and co-production of evidence.
The research is conducted in Uganda at national, district, and community levels. Selected districts provide focal sites for qualitative research, stakeholder dialogues, simulation exercises, and participatory modelling, reflecting variation in health system capacity and epidemic risk. National-level engagement ensures alignment with policy priorities and relevance to planning and epidemic preparedness.
The project will be implemented from August 2025 to July 2028, with workstreams running in parallel and iteratively.
The study is being conducted because most outbreaks in Uganda are geographically constrained in their early phases and require targeted, community-level responses in which community health workers play a central role. Yet policy decisions on community health systems and community health workers' deployment are often made without integrated evidence on system performance, trade-offs, and resilience. By embedding participatory epidemic modelling within real-world governance and planning processes, the project generates actionable evidence to support better decision-making, strengthen epidemic preparedness, and safeguard routine primary health care delivery.
